page.layout: One printed page, one column of running text. Left margin: a few partly cut-off reference marks beside the lines "perquàm periculosas" and "defide-". No right margin text. Running head at top, page number at top left. Bottom edge: show-through from the neighbouring page, left out.

main_text.p: thaginem, contenti ostentatione infus-tationeque superba in portum reverte-runt. Hucusque Appiani verba Latinè reddita. Post quæ dicit, tertio ab hoc eventu die exisse rursum classem Puni-cam, & tunc navale prælium commis-sum esse difficillimum & pertinacissi-mum, fortunaque varium. In cujus prælii descriptione docet, aggerem fuisse ante mœnia Carthaginis spaciosum, portui vicinum, dudum ad excipiendas negotiatorum sarcinas excitatum: & juxta hunc, ne ponendis illic castris (cui rei ob spacium non incommodus erat) à Romanis occuparetur, murum brevem durante hoc bello esse extructum[?]: hunc aggerem, quòd infestando portui, & oppugnandis mœnibus idoneus videretur; post certamen navale ad eundem in multam noctem extractum, à Scipione summâ vi postridie esse appetitum, & in potestatem redactum, mox etiam collocatis ibi machinis variis vim munitionibus urbanis ex eo loco intentari cœpisse: Situm porrò ejus talem fuisse, ut obsessis accessus ad eum ad incendendas hostium machinas urbi perquàm periculosas (cujus rei desiderio vehementer æstuabant) nec terrâ (transitus enim non patebat) nec navibus (erat enim mare ibi vadosum navium.

page.notes: Left margin: partly cut-off marks beside "perquàm periculosas" and "defide-" (possibly reference signs or a note fragment); too faint to read, so not transcribed. "extructum" is doubtful: the printed word has a ligature or circumflex over the e, which I could not read with certainty. "vadosum navium." ends the page; the final word appears to be "navium" from the printed line, which may be a printing error for "navigium" or similar, left as printed. Long s normalised to s; u/v and i/j normalised as instructed.
